headline.title: Gemini Robotics ER 2: powering robotics with video understanding, task orchestration, and multi-robot collaboration
headline.summary: Gemini Robotics has introduced the ER 2, a system designed to enhance robots' capabilities in reasoning, collaboration, and task execution through advanced video understanding and tool orchestration. This development marks a significant advancement in multi-robot collaboration for various robotic applications.

articles.title: Advancing the price-performance frontier with GPT-5.6
articles.summary: OpenAI has introduced lower pricing for its GPT-5.6 models, Luna and Terra, aimed at enhancing cost efficiency for enterprises. The new models are designed to improve the deployment of AI workflows at scale, advancing the price-performance frontier in AI technology.

articles.title: Friend, the lonely AI wearable, returns with a new voice and a much bigger price tag
articles.summary: The AI wearable Friend has been updated to include a new voice feature, allowing it to communicate with users. The device now comes with a significantly higher price tag.

articles.title: Okta buys AI security startup Permiso — source says for about $200M
articles.summary: Okta has acquired AI security startup Permiso for approximately $200 million, enhancing its identity threat detection capabilities. This acquisition aims to help enterprises secure AI agents and non-human identities within cloud environments.

articles.title: LinkedIn actually adds a ‘seems like AI slop’ button
articles.summary: LinkedIn has introduced a new feature allowing users to report posts that appear to be low-quality AI-generated content, labeled as "seems like AI slop." This update is part of LinkedIn's efforts to enhance content quality on the platform.

articles.title: Google says it fixed more Chrome bugs in June than over the past two years, thanks to AI
articles.summary: Google reported that it addressed more Chrome bugs in June than in the previous two years, attributing this increase to the implementation of AI and large language models. This trend reflects a broader industry shift, with companies like Microsoft also leveraging AI tools to enhance their bug detection and resolution processes.

articles.title: LinkedIn adds a button to report AI-generated ‘slop’
articles.summary: LinkedIn is implementing a new reporting option labeled "seems like AI slop" to help users flag low-quality AI-generated content. Additionally, the platform will replace its AI writing feature with a proofreading tool to enhance post quality.

articles.title: Nvidia’s Open Source Alliance Is Missing Some Key Names: OpenAI and Anthropic
articles.summary: Nvidia's Open Source Alliance is notably absent key players such as OpenAI and Anthropic, highlighting ongoing discussions about the open- versus closed-source debate in AI. The latest episode of Uncanny Valley also covers the implications for White House AI policy and privacy concerns regarding chatbot logs.

articles.title: Gemini Robotics 2 Brings Google's AI Into the Physical World
articles.summary: Google DeepMind has released Gemini Robotics 2, an advanced AI model that aims to integrate artificial intelligence into physical environments, marking a notable step towards physical artificial general intelligence (AGI). The deployment of this technology raises concerns regarding the potential risks associated with its real-world applications.

articles.title: Google DeepMind’s new AI model can control a robot’s entire body
articles.summary: Google DeepMind has announced the release of its Gemini Robotics 2 AI model, which can control the entire body of humanoid robots, including movements from feet to fingertips. This advancement builds on the previous model, which was limited to upper body control.

articles.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026’s biggest stage features leaders from Amazon, Replit, Tether, with much more to come
articles.summary: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will showcase prominent leaders from major tech companies, including Amazon, Replit, and Tether, on its main stage. The event continues its tradition of facilitating significant discussions in the technology sector, building on over a decade of history.

articles.title: Chrome Needs Twice-a-Week Patching Thanks to AI Bug Hunting
articles.summary: Google has increased its Chrome patching schedule to twice a week following a significant rise in bug discoveries aided by AI, resulting in more vulnerabilities being addressed than in the previous 23 updates combined. The two updates released in June alone fixed a substantial number of issues, highlighting the effectiveness of AI in identifying security flaws.
